summaries.body:
The 5.0.0 mapping records V4.1.4 as ADDED, SPLIT FROM 4.0.3 V14.5.1. That predecessor required the application server to accept only HTTP methods in use by the application or API, including pre-flight OPTIONS, and to log or alert on requests that were not valid for the application context. The current clause keeps the method-restriction half of that control.

Git events attached to the V4.1.4 ID slot include abhay's 2019-02-11 access-control CWE tagging and authentication-chapter edits. Those are ID-slot reuse; the mapping and V14.5.1 predecessor text are the reliable origin.

On 23 Feb 2019 vanderaj reworded V14.5.1 to resolve #498 (commit 729c18c0). On 7 Jan 2020 janderson updated that same requirement "to include logging support for invalid methods" (commit 29019f6a). The 5.0 split leaves logging and alerting out of V4.1.4; the current text requires only that unused methods be blocked, including OPTIONS during preflight.

Issue snapshots attached here (#376 on logging validation failures, #435 on V8 log-content duplicates, #442 on an old access-control V4.1.1) do not discuss HTTP method restriction. elarlang's 18 Mar 2021 move of V14.5.1 (closes #862) is a later housekeeping event on the predecessor ID, not a wording change to this split clause.
